code_search.description:
Search C++ source code in the current project, the LocoHelperAI plugin, and the UE engine source. Backed by bundled ripgrep. Use this BEFORE guessing property names, spawner IDs, or function signatures - the AI should verify assumptions instead of failing forward.

Operations:
  grep:            raw regex search across files
  find_symbol:     UE-aware lookup of class/function/property/struct/enum by name
  find_references: word-boundary search for usages of a symbol
  read_file:       read a slice of any source file by path + line range

Scope: "project" | "plugin" | "engine" | "all" (default) | absolute path.

Every response reports, for every operation:
  1. The ABSOLUTE roots actually searched, one '#   [scope] <path>' line each. The
     engine root is annotated with its install folder name and the running editor
     version, because a machine can have several engine versions installed and a
     search that lands on the wrong one returns confidently wrong API answers.
     A requested scope whose root does not exist is listed as NOT SEARCHED rather
     than silently dropped, so a missing root never reads as 'no matches'.
  2. Honest counts: 'shown=N total=M'. When results are capped, the header says
     TRUNCATED and a '# TRUNCATED:' line gives the real total from a dedicated
     count pass. If even that pass is capped, the total is reported as unknown
     with a lower bound. A total is never estimated.

context_lines.description: Surrounding context lines per match (-C N, default 0)

kind.description: Symbol kind for find_symbol: any|class|struct|function|property|enum (default any)

max_results.description: Max output match lines (default 50, max 500). Also passed to ripgrep as a PER-FILE --max-count. When either cap bites, the response is marked TRUNCATED and a second count pass reports the true total (or states the total is unknown with a lower bound); a truncated result set can never read as a complete one.

multiline.description: Enable multiline matching (ripgrep --multiline). Default false. Use for patterns that span lines, e.g. 'UPROPERTY\([^)]*\)[^;]*\bName\b'. find_symbol with kind=property enables this automatically.

path.description: File path for read_file (relative-to-scope or absolute)

pattern.description: Regex pattern (grep) or substring symbol name (find_symbol/find_references)

scope.description: Search scope: 'project'|'plugin'|'engine'|'all' (default) or absolute path. The response header lists the ABSOLUTE root(s) this actually resolved to (engine root annotated with install folder + running editor version), and names any requested scope that resolved to nothing as NOT SEARCHED.

download_asset.description: Download a CC0 asset file (zip / texture / model / sound) from a SUPPORTED public host into the project, then extract + import it with execute_python. Supported hosts ONLY (no login needed): Kenney (kenney.nl), PolyHaven (polyhaven.com), AmbientCG (ambientcg.com), OpenGameArt (opengameart.org), and GitHub Releases (github.com / githubusercontent.com). Args: url (a DIRECT download URL on one of those hosts), max_mb (optional size cap, default 100, hard max 500), sha256 (optional expected SHA-256 of the file as 64 hex chars: on mismatch the tool hard-fails AND deletes the download; when omitted the computed digest is printed so you can pin it on the next call). Returns the LOCAL file path on success. NOT supported: Google Drive, Dropbox, Sketchfab, Fab, Quixel / Mixamo, or arbitrary sites - they need auth or are not direct downloads. For those do NOT invent or claim a 'Google Drive MCP' / connector (there is none here); instead ask the user to download the file themselves and give you the LOCAL path, then import it. After a successful download, extract the zip and import via execute_python (Python zipfile + unreal.AssetToolsHelpers.get_asset_tools().import_asset_tasks), then move the results to the requested /Game folder.

max_mb.description: Optional size cap in MB (default 100, hard max 500). The download fails if the file is larger than the cap.

sha256.description: Optional expected SHA-256 digest of the file: exactly 64 hex characters (an optional 'sha256:' prefix is accepted). On mismatch the tool hard-fails and DELETES the downloaded file so a corrupt or tampered payload is never handed to the extract step. When omitted, the computed digest is printed in the result so you can pin it on the next call.

url.description: Direct download URL on a supported CC0 host (kenney.nl, polyhaven.com, ambientcg.com, opengameart.org, github.com / githubusercontent.com).

edit_asset.description: Asset-graph + level-lifecycle operations (use INSTEAD of execute_python for these). Ops (one or more per call): find_referencers {asset: /Game/.. path, confirm_load?: bool} lists packages that reference the asset (read-only preflight before delete/consolidate); asset_metadata {asset, action: get|set|remove|list, tag?, value?} reads/writes asset metadata tags (set auto-saves so the tag survives a restart); new_level {path, partitioned?} and load_level {path} create/open a level (dirty levels are saved first to prevent data loss); consolidate_assets {keep, duplicates:[..], confirm:true} is DESTRUCTIVE - it redirects all references from the duplicates to the keeper and deletes the duplicates, and is GATED behind an explicit confirm:true flag (without it the op only reports what it would do); BOTH paths list each duplicate's current referencers, so the confirm:true call names what it is redirecting from the same scan it acts on (no preview-then-confirm TOCTOU gap); the consolidate itself reports the engine's PER-OBJECT reasons (class mismatch, unregistered asset, partially-consolidated objects) instead of a bare pass/fail; delete_assets {assets:[/Game/.. paths], confirm:true, force?:bool} is DESTRUCTIVE safe-delete - it refuses without confirm:true (listing the plan), refuses on ON-DISK referencers unless force:true (naming them), refuses outright on IN-MEMORY references (release the pin and retry, never delete while pinned), and verifies by asset-registry READBACK rather than trusting the return value; rename_asset {from, to} moves/renames an asset and STATES whether a redirector was left at the old path; duplicate_asset {from, to} copies one and saves the copy; fixup_redirectors {paths?:[..], folder?:/Game/.., recursive?:bool} repoints referencers off ObjectRedirectors and removes the ones that fully fix up (the cleanup step after rename_asset / consolidate_assets). Every op batches, in this order: delete_assets, find_referencers, asset_metadata, new_level, load_level, consolidate_assets, duplicate_asset, rename_asset, fixup_redirectors, save_assets, close_editors - so a single call can rename, clean up the redirector, save, then close the editors. can rename and then clean up the redirector it just created. Unknown argument keys are REFUSED before anything runs, including a misspelled 'confirm' or 'force'. find_referencers, asset_metadata and load_level take their asset as asset, asset_path, path or name; delete_assets and fixup_redirectors take their list as assets, paths, or a single asset string. Every op value is an object {..}; a bare string in its place is refused by name. Mutates assets / the level.

asset_metadata.description: Read/write asset metadata: {asset: /Game/.. path, action: get|set|remove|list, tag?: tag name (get/set/remove), value?: string (set)}. set auto-saves the asset.

close_editors.description: Close asset editor windows: {assets?: [/Game/.. ], all?: true}. 'all' enumerates the open editors and closes them one by one, so the response names WHAT was open. Unreal may prompt for unsaved work, so pair it with save_assets in the same call - save_assets runs first. Useful before a rebuild or a shutdown: an open asset editor is what makes those unsafe.

consolidate_assets.description: DESTRUCTIVE: redirect all references from duplicates to a keeper and delete the duplicates: {keep: /Game/.. , duplicates: [/Game/.. ], confirm: true}. Without confirm:true the op only previews referencer counts and does NOT mutate anything. The referencer scan runs on BOTH paths, so the confirm:true call lists what it is redirecting from the same scan it acts on - no preview-then-confirm TOCTOU gap. The engine refuses the whole consolidate when a duplicate has a DIFFERENT class from the keeper, or when either side is not a registered asset; both are checked and NAMED up front (on the preview arm too), and the consolidate itself reports the per-object results - dirtied packages, objects invalid for consolidation, objects only PARTIALLY consolidated (on which nothing is saved) - plus a per-duplicate readback of whether it is gone or now a redirector to the keeper. Unknown keys (a misspelled 'confirm') are REFUSED before anything runs.

delete_assets.description: DESTRUCTIVE safe-delete: {assets: [/Game/.. ], confirm: true, force?: bool}. Without confirm:true it refuses and lists the plan. Refuses on ON-DISK referencers unless force:true (naming them), and refuses on IN-MEMORY holders it can name (an open editor, a Python global, another loaded asset - release them and retry; never delete while pinned, that is the unrecoverable half-deleted orphan). Engine caches are NOT holders: the Blueprint action database and node template cache are released first, and when the only remaining holder is an engine registry such as the RigVM type registry (which pins every user struct and enum until the asset is gone) the editor's own Force Delete path is taken and reported. Verified by asset-registry readback plus a liveness check, not by the delete return value. Batches with the other ops in the same call. Unknown keys (a misspelled 'confirm' or 'force') are REFUSED before anything is deleted.

duplicate_asset.description: Copy an asset: {from: /Game/.. , to: /Game/.. }. Refuses when the source is missing or the destination already exists. The copy is saved (DuplicateAsset only creates it in memory) and verified by registry readback; the reported path is the one that was actually created.

find_referencers.description: List packages that reference an asset: {asset: /Game/.. path, confirm_load?: bool (load candidates to confirm the hard dependency, slower but accurate)}.

fixup_redirectors.description: Repoint referencers off ObjectRedirectors and delete the ones that fully fix up: {paths?: [/Game/.. redirector paths], folder?: /Game/.. , recursive?: bool (default true)}. Needs at least one of paths / folder; folder sweeps the asset registry for redirectors. A path that is NOT a redirector is refused by name and class rather than silently skipped. Per-redirector readback says which were removed and which REMAIN (a survivor still has a referencer that could not be updated). Run this after rename_asset / consolidate_assets.

load_level.description: Open an existing level: {path: /Game/.. }. Dirty levels are saved first.

new_level.description: Create a new empty level: {path: /Game/.. , partitioned?: bool}. Dirty levels are saved first to prevent data loss.

rename_asset.description: Rename or MOVE an asset: {from: /Game/.. , to: /Game/.. }. A different folder in 'to' is a move - it is the same operation. Refuses when the source is missing or the destination already exists (it never overwrites). Verified by registry readback, and the result STATES whether an ObjectRedirector was left at the old path (it is, whenever something still referenced the asset) so you know to run fixup_redirectors. The engine saves the renamed package and any redirector itself.

save_assets.description: Save packages: {paths?: [/Game/.. ], dirty?: true, dry_run?: bool}. 'dirty' adds every dirty content AND map package, which is what health_check's 'Unsaved packages' report lists. Result is the READ-BACK (IsDirty after the write), not the save call's return value: a package still dirty is reported as STILL DIRTY with the reason when knowable (read-only file). Refuses while PIE is running. dry_run lists what would be written and writes nothing.

edit_data_asset.description: Create and author ANY DataAsset / PrimaryDataAsset instance by class - the data-modeling axis modular gameplay lives on (Lyra AbilitySet / PawnData / ExperienceDefinition / EquipmentDefinition / InputConfig + your own config/balance assets). A data asset is a plain object (no graph, no compile); this tool sets its properties via reflection + ImportText (no gameplay-plugin dependency; works wherever the class exists). Read mode (name only) dumps the class + every non-default property. Mutations (saved + verified): create {class: "/Script/Module.Class" or a bare class name}; set [{property, value}] - a "/Game/..."/"/Script/..." value on an Object/Class property is resolved to the asset and assigned; everything else (scalars, enums, structs, ARRAYS) is applied via ImportText in UE text form (e.g. an AbilitySet grant array: "((Ability=\"...GA_X_C'\",AbilityLevel=1,InputTag=(TagName=\"InputTag.X\")))"). Every set reports a READBACK DIFF - "prop: old -> new" read back off the object (never an echo of the input), and a write that landed on the value already there is tagged UNCHANGED - so a change is auditable and reversible by hand. Soft object/class properties (including ones nested in structs, arrays, sets and maps) are checked against the ASSET REGISTRY without loading anything: a soft path with no registry entry is reported per property as a BROKEN soft reference, the failure mode that otherwise stays silent until it resolves to null at runtime. Read mode reports the same for the whole asset. schema:true (read-only) dumps EVERY editable property with its CPP type, struct members expanded - the discovery pass for valid names and text forms (a wrong 'property' anywhere also comes back with nearest-name suggestions). array_ops edits ONE TArray element at a time - [{property, op: insert|remove|set|move, index, to_index?, value?}], insert appends by default - and map_ops one TMap entry by key - [{property, op: set|remove, key, value?}]. No whole-container re-import: surrounding elements stay untouched, and a value is parsed BEFORE any mutation so a rejected value changes nothing. Mutates the asset.

array_ops.description: Element-level TArray edits that leave the other elements untouched (no whole-array re-import): [{property, op: insert|remove|set|move, index, to_index?, value?}]. insert defaults index to Num (append); set/remove/move require a 0-based in-range index; move also takes to_index and preserves the relative order of everything else. 'value' (insert/set) is the ELEMENT's UE text form, or a /Game or /Script path for object elements; it is parsed BEFORE any mutation, so a rejected value changes nothing. Ops apply in order; an earlier insert/remove shifts the indices later ops see. Each op reports the element read back off the object.

class.description: Class to create (e.g. "/Script/LyraGame.LyraAbilitySet" or a bare class name). Required when creating.

map_ops.description: Entry-level TMap edits addressed by KEY (no whole-map re-import): [{property, op: set|remove, key, value?}]. 'key' is the key type's UE text form; set adds the key or overwrites its value ('value' required, parsed before any mutation); remove hard-fails on a key that is not present, listing the keys that are. Each op reports the entry read back off the object.

name.description: Full /Game/... path of the data asset. With no other argument this is READ mode: dumps the class, every non-default property, and any BROKEN soft references (soft object/class paths with no asset registry entry - they resolve to null at runtime with no warning).

schema.description: Discovery: append a '## Properties' section dumping EVERY editable property of the class with its CPP type (struct members expanded two levels), i.e. the names and shapes 'set'/'array_ops'/'map_ops' accept. Not an operation on its own: passed alone with 'name' the call stays pure READ (nothing dirtied, nothing saved); passed alongside create/set/array_ops/map_ops the section is appended to that report too. A long tree is truncated with the cut stated, never silently.

set.description: Properties to set: [{property, value}]. Object/Class props accept a /Game path; everything else is ImportText UE text. Each entry reports back as "property: old -> new" read off the object, tagged UNCHANGED when the write was a no-op, plus any BROKEN soft reference the property now holds.

edit_material.description: Create, edit, and READ a Material asset deterministically (use INSTEAD of execute_python for material authoring - the Python path has known silent traps). Read mode (name only) dumps blend mode / shading model / two-sided plus every connected property's input expression and all parameters. Mutations (batched, recompiled + saved once): create (bool, auto-implied) makes the Material; properties {blend_mode: Opaque|Masked|Translucent|Additive|Modulate, shading_model: DefaultLit|Unlit|Subsurface|TwoSidedFoliage|ClearCoat|Cloth, two_sided: bool, opacity_mask_clip: number}; usage {skeletal_mesh: bool, instanced_static_meshes: bool, spline_meshes: bool, morph_targets: bool, niagara_sprites: bool, nanite: bool, ...} sets the UMaterial usage flags - a material MISSING the flag for the mesh/particle type it is applied to renders the DEFAULT GREY material at runtime while compiling and previewing fine, so set it whenever you author a material for a skeletal mesh / ISM / spline mesh / Niagara; each flag reports old -> new from read-back and an unknown key is a hard error listing the supported set; clear (bool) deletes ALL expressions (prefer a clean rebuild over incremental repair); add_parameters [{kind: scalar|vector|texture, name, value: number | [r,g,b(,a)] | texture path, connect: BaseColor|Metallic|Specular|Roughness|EmissiveColor|Opacity|OpacityMask|Normal|SubsurfaceColor|AmbientOcclusion|WorldPositionOffset|PixelDepthOffset, output?: source pin, default the default output - pass "A" for texture alpha}]. v2 GRAPH OPS: add_expressions [{class: Multiply|Add|Constant|Constant3Vector|TextureSample|TextureCoordinate|LinearInterpolate|Clamp|BumpOffset|Panner|Fresnel|Power|... (any MaterialExpression subclass by short name), name: call-local handle, properties: {UPROPERTY: value, e.g. ConstA: 2.0, Texture: '/Game/...', Constant: [r,g,b]}}] and connect ["NodeA->NodeB:B", "NodeB->BaseColor"] - format From[:OutputPin]->To[:InputPin]; a target matching a material property name with no node of that name wires the material output. Existing expressions are addressable by object name (see read mode's Graph edges). Every requested connection is VERIFIED by read-back before success is reported, and stale open material editors are closed so the user sees the result on reopen. HLSL TRANSLATION errors (float3->float2 casts, unconnected static-switch inputs, domain restrictions) are surfaced after every recompile and in read mode - wiring can verify and STILL fail translation; fix any '! MATERIAL COMPILE' lines before declaring done. Every mutate ends with an explicit 'translation=OK | FAILED (first error verbatim) | UNAVAILABLE' verdict plus compile_ok=true|false|unknown - UNAVAILABLE/unknown means the status could NOT be read, not that the material is clean. configure_expressions [{name: object name or handle, properties: {...}}] updates properties on EXISTING expressions (the repair primitive - no clear+rebuild needed to fix one flag). screenshot (bool, STANDALONE op): waits for shader compilation, renders a 512px preview sphere of the material and returns it as an IMAGE you can inspect - use it to visually confirm the result after authoring; refuses (listing errors) when the material does not compile. SUBSTRATE (UE5.6 default): read mode reports substrate=ENABLED/disabled. When enabled the lit terminator is FrontMaterial (fed by a Substrate node) and BaseColor/Metallic/Roughness/Normal are INERT - wire connect '<SubstrateNode>->FrontMaterial', or use use_substrate_convert to bridge a legacy/MaterialAttributes graph. FrontMaterial refuses non-Substrate sources (IsResultSubstrateMaterial guard). Mutates the asset.

add_expressions.description: v2: arbitrary expression nodes: [{class: short class name (Multiply, Constant, Constant3Vector, TextureSample, TextureCoordinate, LinearInterpolate, Clamp, BumpOffset, Panner, Fresnel, Power, ...), name: call-local handle used by connect, properties: optional {UPROPERTY: value} map - numbers/bools/strings import directly, [r,g,b(,a)] arrays as colors, /Game/.. strings on object properties load the asset (e.g. Texture)}].

add_parameters.description: Parameter expressions to create: [{kind: scalar|vector|texture, name: parameter name, value: number for scalar | [r,g,b] or [r,g,b,a] for vector | /Game/.. texture path for texture, connect: optional material property to wire the default output into (BaseColor, Roughness, SubsurfaceColor, OpacityMask, Normal, ...), output: optional source pin name when not the default output (e.g. "A" for texture alpha)}].

clear.description: Delete ALL existing expressions before adding (clean rebuild; recommended when repairing).

configure_expressions.description: Set properties on EXISTING material expression nodes (the F73 op) - e.g. a TextureSample's Texture or SamplerType, a Constant's value, a Panner's speed. Array of per-expression objects identifying the node and the properties to set. NOTE: a SamplerType that does not match the bound texture's compression fails translation of the WHOLE material and it renders default grey, so set them together.

connect.description: v2: connection strings "From[:OutputPin]->To[:InputPin]". From/To are add_expressions handles, existing expression object names, or (target only) a material property (BaseColor, Roughness, Normal, ...). OutputPin defaults to the expression's default output; InputPin defaults to the first input (name it for multi-input nodes: A, B, Alpha, Min, Max, ...). Input pins match the EDITOR labels, not internal property names: TextureSample coordinates = 'UVs' (not 'Coordinates'), texture override = 'Tex', Power exponent = 'Exp'. On a miss the error lists the valid names. Each connection is verified by read-back.

create.description: Create the Material if it does not exist (auto-implied when properties/add_parameters is present).

delete_expressions.description: Node names to DELETE from the material graph, e.g. ["Multiply_0", "BaseColorTex"]. Parameter nodes can be named by their ParameterName too. The engine breaks every link to the node and clears any material property it fed, so a delete never leaves a dangling wire. Use this to remove one node; 'clear' still wipes the whole graph.

disconnect.description: Wires to REMOVE, naming the destination (a material input holds exactly one source, so the sink identifies the wire). Two forms: "BaseColor" clears a material property input; "Multiply_0:A" clears one input pin on a node. Runs BEFORE 'connect', so a single call can re-route. Pin names must be EXACT here - unlike 'connect', there is deliberately no closest-match fallback, because guessing on a removal would silently unwire a pin you did not name. A miss lists the node's real input names.

limit.description: v2.2 read pagination: emit at most N lines (0 = all). A continuation line gives the next offset.

name.description: Full asset path to the Material (e.g. /Game/Materials/M_Grass). Read-only when no mutation fields are given.

offset.description: v2.2 read pagination: skip the first N lines.

properties.description: Material-level settings: blend_mode (Opaque|Masked|Translucent|Additive|Modulate), shading_model (DefaultLit|Unlit|Subsurface|TwoSidedFoliage|ClearCoat|Cloth), two_sided (bool), opacity_mask_clip (number).

save.description: Save the asset at the end (default: true).

screenshot.description: Capture the material editor's preview viewport and return it as an image (the F73 op). Pass true. Use to VISUALLY confirm a material edit - a compile success does not prove the material renders (a sampler-type mismatch compiles and then renders default grey).

section.description: v2.2 read pagination: emit ONE section - inputs | expressions | edges | properties. Combine with offset/limit (line window) on big materials; a truncated response means data was LOST - page instead.

stats.description: Report the material's compiled shader statistics (instruction counts, texture samplers, etc.). Pass true to read. Use to check a material fits a platform budget after editing it.

terse.description: v2.2: suppress per-item success echo on mutations (keeps failures + final summary). USE ON BIG BATCHES (100+ nodes) - otherwise the response cap can truncate away the summary line.

usage.description: UMaterial usage flags, {key: bool} - which mesh / particle types this material may be applied to. A material MISSING the flag for the type it is used on renders the DEFAULT GREY material at runtime even though it compiles and previews correctly, so set it whenever you author for a skeletal mesh, instanced static mesh, spline mesh, morph targets or Niagara. Each flag is reported old -> new by read-back; an unknown key is a hard error. Supported keys: skeletal_mesh, static_lighting, morph_targets, spline_meshes, instanced_static_meshes, particle_sprites, beam_trails, mesh_particles, niagara_sprites, niagara_ribbons, niagara_mesh_particles, geometry_collections, geometry_cache, clothing, water, hair_strands, lidar_point_cloud, virtual_heightfield_mesh, nanite, volumetric_cloud, heterogeneous_volumes, static_mesh, voxels.

use_substrate_convert.description: E06 (Substrate only): bridge a legacy PBR / MaterialAttributes graph into the Substrate FrontMaterial terminator. Pass the add_expressions handle / object name of a node that produces material attributes (e.g. a MakeMaterialAttributes node). Spawns a SubstrateConvertMaterialAttributes node, sets bUseMaterialAttributes + ShadingModel=DefaultLit, wires source->Convert->FrontMaterial, and verifies the FrontMaterial sink by read-back. No-op error on non-Substrate projects (use connect '->BaseColor' there). Object form {source, output?} also accepted.

edit_material_function.description: Author a standalone UMaterialFunction asset (E34) - the reusable building-block half of a material library (shared noise/masking/UV/utility logic). Core-engine, no plugin gate. name (required, /Game path). The function is created when missing ONLY if the call carries an authoring arg (function_inputs, function_outputs, add_expressions, connections or description); a name-only call on a missing path FAILS not-found and creates nothing (F428). description (optional). function_inputs [{name, type, sort?}] where type = scalar(default)|vector2|vector3|vector4|texture2d|texturecube|staticbool|bool|materialattributes - a function with NO typed signature exposes zero pins. function_outputs [{name, sort?}]; if neither inputs nor outputs are given on create, one default "Result" output is added. add_expressions [{class, name}] (class = short name like "Multiply"/"Constant"/"TextureSample"; name is a connection handle). connections ["From->To", "From:OutPin->To:InPin"] using handles; signature nodes are referenced as "Input:<name>" / "Output:<name>" (bare Input/Output = the first one). Read mode (name only) dumps the expression count + the input/output signature; it creates nothing, dirties nothing and saves nothing, and on a path that does NOT exist it FAILS not-found instead of manufacturing the asset, so it is a safe way to probe a path (F428). Every create is therefore part of a write call, and write mode always ends in a save, so "+ Created MaterialFunction" means created ON DISK. Mutates the asset. Layer/Blend usage, the material-function INSTANCE, the layer STACK,and binding the function INTO a material are separate ops, not this tool.

add_expressions.description: [{class, name, properties?}] - UMaterialExpression subclasses by short name (e.g. "Multiply"); name is the connection handle. properties applies UPROPERTY values via the same applier as edit_material (T-052). connections can also address EXISTING expressions by object name (e.g. MaterialExpressionConstant_0) and signature nodes via Input:<name>/Output:<name> in follow-up calls (T-054).

connections.description: ["From->To", "From:OutPin->To:InPin"] using expression handles; signature nodes as "Input:<name>" / "Output:<name>".

function_inputs.description: [{name, type, sort?}] - typed input pins. type = scalar(default)|vector2|vector3|vector4|texture2d|texturecube|staticbool|bool|materialattributes.

function_outputs.description: [{name, sort?}] - output pins. Defaults to one "Result" output on create if no signature is given.

name.description: Full /Game/... path. The UMaterialFunction is created when missing ONLY if the call carries an authoring arg (function_inputs / function_outputs / add_expressions / connections / description). Pass name ALONE for read mode: it dumps the expression count + signature, creates nothing and saves nothing, and FAILS not-found on a path that does not exist (F428).

edit_material_instance.description: Author a MaterialInstanceConstant (MIC) - the standard way material VARIATIONS ship (a parent material + a few overridden parameters). edit_material builds the parent UMaterial graph; this builds the cheap instances. name (required, /Game path, created if missing). parent (required on create, /Game or /Engine path of a UMaterial or MIC; also re-parents). scalars [{name, value}]; vectors [{name, value:[r,g,b,a] or "(R=..,G=..,B=..,A=..)"}]; textures [{name, value:"/Game/..."}]. static_switches [{name, value:true|false}] flips the parent's STATIC SWITCH parameters (the feature toggles marketplace and engine parent materials gate their branches on, previously neither discoverable nor settable here); each flip compiles a NEW shader permutation for the instance, so the whole batch is validated BEFORE any parameter is written and an unknown switch name refuses the call outright, listing the parent's valid switch names. Reports per switch 'value before -> value after [inherited|overridden -> inherited|overridden]' read back off the asset. set_material_layers {layers:[func paths], blends:[func paths]} assigns a Material Attribute Layers stack (layers[0]=background, blends.length=layers.length-1), round-tripped via GetMaterialLayers. clear {scalars:[names], vectors:[names], textures:[names]} REMOVES the per-instance override so the parameter reverts to the parent value (without it an instance can only accumulate overrides); it runs AFTER the scalars/vectors/textures sets in the same call, and reports 'before -> parent value now in effect' per parameter. Read mode (name only) dumps the parent + its available scalar/vector/texture/static-switch parameter names, their current values, and whether each is overridden or inherited. Mutates the asset.

clear.description: F3-14.3: REMOVE per-instance overrides so the parameters revert to the parent value. {scalars:[names], vectors:[names], textures:[names]} - plain name arrays, not {name,value} objects. Runs AFTER the scalars/vectors/textures sets in the same call. Reports 'overridden value BEFORE -> parent value now in effect' per parameter. A name that is not currently overridden is reported as skipped (not an error); a name that exists neither as an override nor on the parent is an error with nearest-name suggestions.

name.description: Full /Game/... path of the MaterialInstanceConstant (created if missing).

parent.description: Parent material path (/Game or /Engine UMaterial or MIC). Required on create.

set_material_layers.description: E06: assign Material Attribute Layers. {layers:[MaterialFunction paths], blends:[MaterialFunction paths]}. layers[0] is the background layer (no blend); each later layer[i] pairs with blends[i-1], so blends.length must equal layers.length-1. Round-trips via GetMaterialLayers. Parent must be a layered material.

static_switches.description: 14.4: static switch overrides: [{name, value:true|false}]. 'value' must be a JSON bool literal - strings ("true") and numbers (1) are REFUSED because they coerce silently and a wrong switch picks the wrong shader branch. Flipping a switch compiles a NEW shader permutation for this instance, so the whole batch is validated before ANY parameter is written: an unknown switch name, a missing 'name', a non-bool 'value' or an empty array refuses the call with nothing applied and lists the parent's valid switch names. Reports before -> after values plus the inherited/overridden transition, read back off the asset. Read mode (name only) lists the parent's static switches with their current values.

edit_texture.description: Set build/import settings on existing UTextures (does NOT import). TARGET: pass exactly ONE of name (/Game path to one texture) | names (["/Game/..."] array) | folder (/Game/... folder, scanned RECURSIVELY for every UTexture in it). A batch over 100 textures is REFUSED, never silently truncated, and one unloadable path refuses the whole call before anything is written. preset (semantic bundle applied BEFORE explicit args so explicit args override: normal_map = TC_Normalmap + srgb off; mask = TC_Masks + srgb off; ui = TC_Default + srgb on + TEXTUREGROUP_UI; hdr = TC_HDR + srgb off; unknown preset is a hard error). compression (TextureCompressionSettings: TC_Default | TC_Normalmap | TC_Masks | TC_Grayscale | TC_HDR | TC_Alpha | ...). srgb (bool). lod_group (TextureGroup: TEXTUREGROUP_World | _UI | _Character | _Effects | ...). filter (TF_Default | TF_Nearest | TF_Bilinear | TF_Trilinear). mip_gen (TMGS_FromTextureGroup | TMGS_SimpleAverage | TMGS_NoMipmaps | ...). lod_bias (int). Read mode (target only, no mutating args) dumps dimensions, source size, pixel format, virtual streaming, the required sampler type plus every setting, does NOT modify or save the asset, and emits a condensed #json-texture: line for one texture or a #json-textures: array for a batch. Write mode properly rebuilds each texture (PostEditChange) so the change takes, reports every setting as a read-back 'old -> new' (or 'already X (no change)'), and BEFORE the change lands it NAMES the materials whose TextureSample SamplerType will no longer match, with the exact edit_material fix: a compression/srgb/lod_group change that breaks a sampler makes the WHOLE material render default grey (F94). That scan is shallow (asset-registry referencers, UMaterial only, 50 materials per call) and says so. A batch write emits one block per texture plus a '= BATCH:' summary and only FAILS when no texture changed at all. Common fix: a normal map left at TC_Default+sRGB looks washed out -> preset=normal_map. Mutates the assets (write mode only).

folder.description: Batch: /Game/... folder, scanned RECURSIVELY for every UTexture in it. Mutually exclusive with name and names. Refused above 100 textures, and refused when it resolves to 0.

name.description: Full /Game/... path to an existing UTexture. Mutually exclusive with names and folder.

names.description: Batch: array of /Game/... texture paths. Mutually exclusive with name and folder. Refused above 100 entries; a path that does not load refuses the whole call before anything is written.

preset.description: Semantic settings bundle applied before explicit args (explicit args override): normal_map | mask | ui | hdr.

virtual_texture_streaming.description: Stream this texture as a Virtual Texture (UTexture::VirtualTextureStreaming). Read mode reports it as virtual_texture_streaming.

execute_python.description:
Execute Python code in UE Editor. Pass the source inline as 'code', or pass 'file' with the path to a .py script instead - exactly one is needed ('file' wins if you send both). 'import unreal' and loco helpers are auto-imported. Helpers: setup_overlap(comp), setup_block(comp), get_component(actor,'Name'), set_props(obj, prop=val), find_actor('Label'), spawn(path, [x,y,z]), list_props(obj), list_components(actor), describe(obj), load_bp(path), compile_bp(bp). Use for: collision config, property changes, spawning, batch ops, anything C++ tools can't do. The interpreter namespace PERSISTS across calls, so any global left bound to a UObject pins that object for the session and blocks a later delete of its asset; the result footer names every new holder this call created (`UObject pin report`) so you can `del` it in your next call.

PREFER THE HELPERS OVER RAW unreal.* APIs. They are verified against this exact engine build; guessed API names are the single largest source of failures here (measured over 15 days of production: AttributeError/TypeError/NameError in generated code account for more failures than any other cause). `help(loco.<name>)` is free - only the result returns to you - so check a signature instead of guessing it.

APIs that LOOK right and are WRONG on UE 5.6+, verified:
  unreal.EditorActorSubsystem() - deprecated, warns every call. Use spawn(path,[x,y,z]), or unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.EditorActorSubsystem).
  unreal.EditorRequestBeginPlay / EditorRequestEndPlay - do NOT exist. Use start_pie() / stop_pie(); start_pie is ASYNC, poll pie_ready() in a LATER call.
  unreal.AnimationBlueprintLibrary - removed. Use the edit_anim_asset tool.

THESE HARD-CRASH THE EDITOR - no exception is raised and unsaved work is lost:
  Spawning a particle/Niagara/Emitter actor from Python. Import the asset only; let the user place it.
  Reading an OPEN sequencer range bound (get_start_frame/get_end_frame/get_range) without first checking has_start_frame()/has_end_frame(). Prefer the edit_level_sequence tool.
  Destroying every actor to clear a level also destroys the Builder Brush (its class is 'Brush'), after which the next save asserts and closes the editor. Keep 'Brush' alongside 'WorldSettings' in any keep-list. Wingman now rebuilds it and tells you, but do not rely on that.

code.description: Python code to execute. Pass this OR 'file' - at least one is required, and 'file' wins when both are given. Use 'import unreal' for UE APIs. Example: unreal.EditorAssetLibrary.save_asset('/Game/BP_MyActor'). Runs in the editor's PERSISTENT interpreter namespace - globals survive between calls, so any global left holding an unreal.Object pins it for the session and blocks a later delete of its asset. The result carries a 'UObject pin report' footer naming every new holder this call created; 'del <name>' in your NEXT call releases it.

file.description: Path to a Python 3 script file to execute (absolute, or relative to the project directory; UTF-8; 2 MB cap). A file-only call is fully supported: pass this OR 'code' (at least one is required), and this one wins when both are passed. Use for multi-line scripts - the file path avoids every JSON/transport escaping layer that mangles inline code.

mode.description: Execution mode: 'file' (default, multi-line script, side effects) or 'eval' (a single expression whose value-repr is returned in command_result with no print needed). Note: 'eval' must be ONE expression; loco helpers / multi-line setup must run in a prior 'file' call (module imports persist in the interpreter).

explore.description: Search project files, assets, and code. Use 'path' with /Game/ for asset search, 'query' for text search. Filters AND together: 'path' scopes, 'pattern' globs the name, 'query' substring-matches the name, 'type' narrows the asset class - pass a FULL class path (e.g. /Script/Engine.StaticMesh) for an exact registry-level class filter that includes subclasses, or a loose name (e.g. 'texture') for substring class matching. Use 'filter' for Blueprint-specific search (by parent, component, interface). Every listing reports shown=N total=T (a capped page never reads as complete), tags asset rows that are currently in memory with 'loaded' (untagged rows are registry-only - explore does not load them), and ends with a #json-explore: line carrying the same rows. Always explore before editing to find correct asset paths.

context.description: Lines of context around code matches (0-10, default: 2)

limit.description: Max rows PER PAGE, 1-200 (default: 50). Caps rows shown, not the reported total.

offset.description: Pagination offset (default: 0). Every listing header reports shown=N total=T so a capped page is never mistaken for the whole set.

path.description: Directory or /Game asset path to search. Scope filter - ANDs with pattern/query/type.

pattern.description: Glob on the NAME (e.g., *.cpp, BP_*, *Door*). ANDs with path/query/type.

query.description: On /Game paths: case-insensitive substring of the ASSET NAME. On disk paths: text searched inside files. ANDs with path/pattern/type.

type.description: Class/kind filter. Loose name ('texture', 'blueprints') = case-insensitive substring of the asset CLASS name. A FULL class path ('/Script/Engine.StaticMesh') = exact registry-level class filter INCLUDING subclasses, and routes to the asset registry even with no 'path'. For disk paths: files, folders, both.

read_bp.description: Read Blueprint structure: variables, components, graphs, nodes, connections, interfaces. Use 'include' to select sections. Use 'graph' to read nodes in detail with GUIDs. Always read before editing. Use explore to find asset paths first. include=["selected"] returns the node(s) the user has selected in the open Blueprint editor right now (for 'fix/explain this node'); in that mode 'name' may be empty to mean 'whichever Blueprint graph the user is looking at'. include=["defaults"] dumps the compiled CDO property snapshot - the readback pair for edit_blueprint set_class_defaults.

event_source.description: Optional: when include contains 'events', scope the listing to this widget or component name. Omit to list all bindable delegates across the Blueprint.

graph.description: Specific graph name to read in detail (e.g., EventGraph)

include.description: Sections to include: summary, variables, components, graphs, interfaces, events, widgets, bindings, selected, functions, defaults, timelines, widget_details. 'widgets' = a WidgetBlueprint's UMG tree (name, class, slot, Text) - also shown in the default summary for WidgetBlueprints. 'bindings' = F98 Accessed-None pre-flight: cross-checks each graph-referenced widget variable against the tree (widget exists + is Is Variable). 'selected' = the user's current node selection in the open Blueprint editor (use for 'fix/explain this node'); with 'selected', 'name' may be empty. 'functions' = per-function flags (pure/net/reliable/access/const/thread_safe) plus the full signature: param rows (in/out, type, default, [by-ref]) and function-local variables, with a condensed #json-functions line; the readback pair for edit_blueprint add_functions. 'defaults' = one line per editable CDO property ('name (Type) = value') plus a condensed #json-defaults line; the readback pair for edit_blueprint set_class_defaults.

limit.description: PER-SECTION line budget (default 100, max 1000) - each graph's node list gets its OWN budget, and so does each graph's connection dump (it is not a shared total across sections). F432: connections are BOUNDED by this too; they used to ignore it and dump every edge. A '# MORE offset=N remaining=M' marker appears when a section pages; the connection dump's marker reads '# MORE connections offset=N remaining=M', and its header reads '# CONNECTIONS <graph> <total> shown=<n> offset=<n>' so you can always see total vs shown.

offset.description: Pagination offset (default: 0). Applies to EVERY paged section independently, including each graph's connection dump (F432).

take_viewport_screenshot.description: Capture the active Level Editor or PIE/game viewport as a JPEG image. Use after visual changes (actor placement, lighting, materials) or to verify gameplay during PIE. Returns base64 image. Refuses to capture Blueprint / asset-editor preview viewports - if no Level Editor or PIE viewport is available, returns a clear error so the assistant cannot falsely claim visual verification of a level. Pass return_image:false to save the JPEG to Saved/LocoHelperAI/ViewportShots/ and get the file path plus capture metadata instead of the base64 payload - recommended for an external MCP caller that only wants the file. Optional one-frame camera override: camera_location [X,Y,Z], camera_rotation [Pitch,Yaw,Roll] in degrees, and fov (5-170 horizontal degrees). The Level Editor camera is moved for THIS capture only and restored on every exit path, so framing a shot no longer requires loco.frame_actor to permanently move the user's view. The override is refused while PIE is the capture target (that view comes from the player camera) and hard-fails when the viewport's read-back camera does not match the request, so a correctly-encoded image of the wrong angle can never be returned. With return_image:true the applied camera is in the tool log (read_logs); return_image:false puts it in the text result. Args: {return_image? (default true), focus_actor?, focus_margin?, camera_location?, camera_rotation?, fov?}. focus_actor frames a level actor by Outliner label and is the one-call way to screenshot something you just spawned.

camera_location.description: Optional [X, Y, Z] world location to frame this ONE capture from. The Level Editor camera is moved for the capture and restored before the tool returns, so the user's view is never left moved. Refused while PIE is the capture target. Must be exactly 3 JSON numbers.

camera_rotation.description: Optional [Pitch, Yaw, Roll] camera rotation in degrees for this ONE capture. The order is Pitch, Yaw, Roll - NOT the (Roll, Pitch, Yaw) order that UE's Python unreal.Rotator() positional constructor uses, which silently aims the camera at the ground. Restored with the rest of the camera.

focus_actor.description: Outliner label of a LEVEL ACTOR to frame, e.g. 'BP_Coin_2'. Computes a bounds-scaled 3/4 view and points the camera at it, then restores your viewport like any other override here. Resolves exact label first, then case-insensitive substring over label + internal name. Frames on COLLIDING bounds when they are tighter, so a Character is framed on its body and not on its perception sphere. Mutually exclusive with camera_location / camera_rotation, which it would otherwise silently overwrite. An ASSET is not framable this way - this is level actors only.

focus_margin.description: Distance multiplier for focus_actor (default 1.0 = the standard 3/4 view; >1 pulls the camera back for context, <1 tightens). Ignored without focus_actor.

fov.description: Optional horizontal field of view in degrees for this ONE capture, 5 to 170. Lower = tighter framing on a distant actor. Restored with the rest of the camera.

return_image.description: Default true: return the capture inline as IMAGE_BASE64:jpeg:<payload>. false = write the JPEG to Saved/LocoHelperAI/ViewportShots/ and return the saved file path plus the capture metadata only - recommended for external callers, where the payload is pure token cost (T-258).

vault_asset.description:
List and install content the user ALREADY OWNS from the Epic Games Launcher vault - the Fab and Marketplace packs they have bought and downloaded. Fully offline: no account, no API key, no network call.

USE THIS FIRST when the user asks for an asset they might already have ("a concrete material", "a medieval sword", "a rock pack"). It costs nothing, needs no credentials and is instant, unlike generating one.

action='list' reports every vault entry: its name, the Fab listing it came from, its type, size, file count and whether it can be installed. action='install' with 'name' copies that entry's content into the project under /Game and rescans the asset registry.

Only ASSET PACKS install. A vault entry that is a whole PROJECT or a PLUGIN is refused by name, because copying only its Content folder silently drops its Config and leaves a broken half-install - but force=true copies just its Content anyway when the user asks, with a warning naming what was left behind. Pass dry_run=true first to see exactly what would be written.

It CANNOT search or download from Fab - only what is already on this machine.

dry_run.description: [install] Report what would be copied without writing anything (default false).

filter.description: [list] Only show entries whose name contains this text, case-insensitive.

force.description: [install] Install an entry that is NOT an AssetPack (a Project or plugin) by copying only its Content (default false). The Config folder and .uproject are not copied, so the assets may reference settings this project lacks. Only pass this when the user has asked for it after being told what is left behind.

name.description: [install] The vault entry to install, as the 'entry' value printed by action=list. A case-insensitive partial match is accepted when it is unambiguous.
